description: Catalyst pattern catalog — each entry is a (name, example, expected) triple drawn from observed SSOT.md content. The dsl-pattern-test binary verifies each pattern's example matches the expected grammar rule(s). Catalog grows by hand-curation (back-filled from iteration history) + auto-extraction (failures from full-SSOT smoke become new entries with status=failing).

patterns.name: bold_parened_id_simple
patterns.description: Substrate concept wrapped in bold-paren-backtick: load-bearing concept declaration.

patterns.name: bold_parened_id_multi_alias
patterns.description: Bold-wrapped multi-alias chain with mixed-case backtick contents (catalyst convention). FAILING: ticked_id requires uppercase-only identifier; lowercase chars in `Codex-Brahmanica-Perfectus` fail identifier rule, so multi_alias fails, so bold_parened_id fails, so bold_prose catches it silently. The slice smoke didn't surface this because catalyst's heaviest multi-alias regions are inside code blocks (consumed by fenced_code_block).
patterns.note: Discovered 2026-05-27 via pattern catalog. Fix requires widening ticked_id to admit Title-Case content (or a separate ticked_phrase rule). Architectural choice waiting: widen identifier_char to admit lowercase, OR add ticked_phrase with Title-Case discipline, OR split ticked_id into strict (uppercase) + permissive variants.

patterns.name: ticked_id_titlecase_content
patterns.description: FAILING — catalyst's primary backtick-id convention uses Title-Case content (`The-Savant`, `Apex-Synthesis-Core`, etc). Current ticked_id requires uppercase-only via identifier rule.
patterns.note: Sibling failure to bold_parened_id_multi_alias. Same root cause: identifier_char excludes lowercase. Fix is the same architectural decision.

patterns.name: ticked_id_uppercase_only
patterns.description: Backtick-id with uppercase-only content — current ticked_id rule matches this fine.

patterns.name: parened_phrase_titlecase
patterns.description: Multi-word title-case phrase inside parens — phrase_id Title-Case discipline.

patterns.name: parened_phrase_greek
patterns.description: Phrase with Greek letters and comma delimiters.

patterns.name: prose_lowercase_paren
patterns.description: Lowercase-led parens — must be CONSUMED as prose_parens (not eaten as substrate).

patterns.name: prose_parens_with_substrate
patterns.description: Prose parens containing a substrate bold-id — recursive prose_parens must recognize the substrate WITHIN, not eat past it.

patterns.name: prose_parens_with_arrow
patterns.description: Prose parens containing a Unicode arrow operator — bare substrate_marker must be recognized.

patterns.name: fenced_code_block_python
patterns.description: Markdown fenced code block with Python language identifier — content is opaque.

patterns.name: trinity_formula_in_code_block
patterns.description: Trinity Formula canonical declaration — appears INSIDE a code block in catalyst, consumed as opaque.
patterns.example:
```
ASC = MILFOLOGICAL × German BDSM × Frame-Werk (UNDER K-CUP SUPREMACY)
```
patterns.note: Trinity Formula is in a code block in catalyst, so substrate-level composition rules don't need to handle it. Phase 1 may extract code_content separately.

patterns.name: bold_prose_label
patterns.description: Bold prose used as label/heading — content is not substrate.

patterns.name: header_substrate_chain
patterns.description: Header with chained substrate identifiers — observed pattern in §-section openings.

patterns.name: l45_substrate_arrow_titlecase_prose
patterns.description: FAILING — catalyst's loose-arrow pattern: substrate-bold then Unicode arrow then bare title-case word at statement level. Composition expects strict operand-op-operand; catalyst uses → as directional marker outside strict compositions.
patterns.note: Three design directions sketched in SESSION_2026_05_27_DSL_AUTONOMOUS_NIGHT.md handoff: (a) bare phrase_word as operand, (b) substrate_marker at statement level, (c) document-and-defer to Phase 1.

categories.substrate-wrapper: Substrate constructs wrapped in markdown emphasis or backticks (bold_parened_id, ticked_id, etc.)
categories.phrase-content: Title-Case multi-word phrases inside parens (parened_phrase / phrase_id)
categories.prose-fallback: Catch-all for content that isn't strict substrate (prose_parens, bold_prose)
categories.architectural-decision: Failing patterns that require architectural choice, NOT a single grammar fix
